projects.name: AI Hub Project
projects.description:
A two-part workspace for AI leadership work. The parent folder contains two subprojects that serve different purposes but share the same overall mission.

ai-hub/ is a private content workspace for preparing and developing AI training material, standards, and workshops. It is organized by audience skill tier (beginner, intermediate, advanced) and covers learning material creation, standards and protocols, workshop planning, personal skill development, and tooling resources. It is a document/markdown workspace, not a deployable application.

ai-hub-platform/ is a Next.js 16 web application for creating, managing, and presenting AI training material. It provides a dashboard view and a presentation mode. The app uses server components by default, Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui, Zod for validation, Framer Motion for animations, and next-themes for dark/light mode toggling. A Prisma-backed Postgres database is planned but not yet connected.

projects.name: baby-claw
projects.description:
A TypeScript/Node.js agent harness - a boilerplate for building focused "sniper agents" that outperform generalist agents by staying lean and purpose-built. Inspired by the OpenClaw teardown.

The core insight is that generalist agents (like OpenClaw) accumulate context rot - starting at ~7,000 tokens of fixed overhead and ballooning to ~45,000 tokens after months of use, causing up to 40% performance degradation. A sniper agent starts at ~1,400 tokens and stays lean because it only loads what it needs.

Every agent is defined by four things: Triggers (cron, heartbeat, webhook, CLI/HTTP), Context injection (`SOUL.md` personality, `AGENTS.md` config, `MEMORY.md` persistent facts, JSONL conversation history, tool schemas), Tools (what creates the agentic loop - LLM calls tool, gets result, decides next step), and Outputs (how the agent communicates and writes to the world).

The harness itself is the reusable infrastructure. Each new agent is just a configuration: a `SOUL.md` + a specific tool set + a trigger. Uses the Vercel AI SDK (model-agnostic, 2M+ weekly downloads) rather than the OpenAI Agents SDK (too new, broken Gemini adapter) or LangGraph (too much magic). All models route through OpenRouter to avoid EU regional restrictions on Google's free tier.
projects.description_short: A TypeScript/Node.js agent harness - a boilerplate for building focused "sniper agents" that outperform generalist agents by staying lean and purpose-built.
projects.hosting: Railway (baby-claw app). Mattermost self-hosted on homelab or Hetzner.

run_commands.pnpm dev: run the harness with tsx (hot reload via tsx)

projects.notes: No Claude via Anthropic direct - too expensive. Preferred models: `openrouter/google/gemini-2.0-flash-001` for routine tasks (~$0.075/1M tokens), `openrouter/openai/gpt-4o-mini` for complex reasoning. Local/private: Ollama. Gemini 2.0 Flash has a 1M token context window, making context rot nearly a non-issue for routine agents. Agent behavior is configured in markdown files (`SOUL.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `MEMORY.md`), not in compiled code. SDK decision log is in CLAUDE.md.

projects.name: Clean Slate
projects.description:
A personal project dashboard that auto-syncs from ~/Documents/. Shows every project you work on in a compact, expandable list with everything you need to orient yourself: what the project does, its tech stack, how to run it, where it's hosted, and which accounts it uses.

The dashboard reads from CLEAN-SLATE.md files placed in each project's root folder. A sync script scans ~/Documents/, parses these files along with package.json and git config, and writes the combined data to config/data.json. The Next.js app reads this at build time and renders a dark, monospace, dense UI - no fluff, just information.

A macOS launchd job runs the sync automatically on a schedule. When data.json changes, it auto-commits and pushes, and Vercel deploys the update. You never have to remember to sync manually.
projects.description_short: A personal project dashboard that auto-syncs from ~/Documents/.
projects.hosting: Vercel free tier. Domain: ops.hosk.app (or similar subdomain of hosk.app).
projects.notes:
No database. Fully static. Data comes exclusively from CLEAN-SLATE.md files in project folders.
To add a new project to the dashboard, create a CLEAN-SLATE.md in that project's root.

projects.name: Company Knowledge Base
projects.description:
A multi-user knowledge base with semantic search and RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) over internal company documents. Users log in via Google Sign-In or email/password and are placed in a `pending` state until an admin assigns a role.

The core flow is: uploaded documents get chunked and embedded locally using `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` (384-dim vectors), then stored in Qdrant for vector search. When a user asks a question, the app retrieves the most relevant chunks from Qdrant, passes them to an LLM via OpenRouter, and streams the answer back. All conversations are persisted in PostgreSQL.

Documents are organized into Collections (e.g. HR, Engineering). Each collection maps to a dedicated Qdrant collection. Role-based access controls which collections a user can search. Roles: `admin`, `editor`, `member`, `pending`.

The admin panel covers document upload, collection CRUD, user management, model selection, a KB description editor, and external connectors (Google Drive integration exists in code but needs end-to-end testing).
projects.description_short: A multi-user knowledge base with semantic search and RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) over internal company documents.
projects.hosting: App: Coolify on Hetzner server, live at **https://kb.stormfors.ai** (Coolify app UUID: `mk8k08soks4s48wcs84gssoo`). Database: PostgreSQL managed via Coolify on the same server. Qdrant: Docker container on the same Coolify internal network.

run_commands.npx prisma migrate deploy: Apply pending migrations (run in Coolify terminal after deploy)
run_commands.npx prisma db seed: Seed the database (first deploy / full reset only)

projects.notes:
- Deploy by pushing to main - Coolify auto-deploys via GitHub webhook
- Embedding runs locally inside the container using `@xenova/transformers` - no external embedding API needed
- After any Prisma schema change: create migration locally, deploy, then run `npx prisma migrate deploy` in Coolify terminal
- Default LLM model: `qwen/qwen-2.5-7b-instruct` via OpenRouter
- See `TASKS.md` for known issues and pending work
- Reference repo (read-only): `~/Desktop/private-knowledge-base`

projects.name: Health Insights Tracker (React Native)
projects.description:
A voice-first personal health tracking mobile app targeting App Store publication. Users log lifestyle factors and symptoms daily; the app combines statistical analysis with LLM interpretation to surface trustworthy correlations and insights. This is a mobile rebuild of the Next.js web app at `/Users/hanna/Documents/tracker` - portable code (metric definitions, Zod schemas, LLM prompts, date utils) should be reused from there.

Privacy is a hard constraint - Supabase Row-Level Security is required on every user-scoped table. Hanna is the admin (can manage metrics and settings, cannot see other users' data). UX must be simple - one user is not tech-savvy. The app is offline-first: entry logging works via local SQLite and syncs to Supabase when online.

LLM calls happen in Supabase Edge Functions (not client-side) to keep API keys server-side. Architecture, code quality, and UX should meet App Store review standards from the start.
projects.description_short: A voice-first personal health tracking mobile app targeting App Store publication.
stack: Supabase (auth + PostgreSQL + RLS + Edge Functions + real-time)
projects.hosting: Supabase (EU region, database + auth + edge functions). App distributed via App Store (iOS target). No separate server.
projects.notes: Uses `@shopify/flash-list` instead of FlatList and `expo-image` instead of RN Image for performance. Target 60fps on all animations and lists. Apple/Google sign-in prepared for later (not in initial build). Charts: `react-native-gifted-charts` or Victory Native. Reference the web app's `docs/REQUIREMENTS.md` and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` for full feature requirements and data model - adapt Prisma schema to Supabase SQL migrations.

Each user logs daily lifestyle factors (food, sleep, weather, stress, etc.) and symptoms (bloating, palpitations, blood pressure, fatigue, brain fog, etc.). An AI analysis pipeline finds patterns and correlations between logged factors and symptoms.

Privacy is a hard requirement - the two users have strict data isolation and cannot see each other's entries. Hanna is the admin and can manage tracked metric categories and system settings, but cannot see the other user's health data. The UX must be simple - one user is not tech-savvy and needs clear flows with obvious next actions.

Voice input with AI extraction is the primary entry method. Manual forms are the fallback. The app includes an option to cross-reference findings with online medical sources. This is the web version; a React Native mobile rebuild lives at `/Users/hanna/Documents/rn-health-tracker`.

projects.name: JSON-LD Schema Generator
projects.description:
An internal Stormfors tool that automates the creation of JSON-LD structured data and llms.txt files for any website. The pipeline works in stages: it discovers pages via a sitemap, crawls each page using the Firecrawl API, sends the content to an LLM (via OpenRouter) to generate appropriate schema markup, validates the output against schema.org rules, auto-fixes any errors, then presents the results with copy/export buttons.

Each run is associated with a client record and is stored in PostgreSQL so runs can be revisited. A Trello comment integration allows generated reports to be posted back to Trello cards. The tool also generates llms.txt files - a machine-readable index of a site's content for LLM consumption.
projects.description_short: An internal Stormfors tool that automates the creation of JSON-LD structured data and llms.txt files for any website.
projects.hosting: Deployed on Coolify (Stormfors Hetzner server) at `aeo.stormfors.ai`. Build pack is Dockerfile (not nixpacks). Standalone PostgreSQL database (`json-ld-db`). The container entrypoint runs `prisma db push` and a slug backfill script on startup. There is no local database - DB operations require the deployed container.

run_commands.pnpm dev: start Next.js dev server on port 3000
run_commands.pnpm prisma generate: regenerate Prisma Client after schema changes

projects.notes: Prisma 7 has specific quirks: `prisma.config.ts` uses `process.env.DATABASE_URL ?? ''` (not `env()` - breaks Docker builds), `schema.prisma` has no `url` in the datasource block, and there is no `--skip-generate` flag. Prisma CLI is installed in an isolated `/prisma-cli` directory in Docker because pnpm symlinks break between build stages. Detailed deployment writeup lives at `~/knowledge-base/issues-solved/nextjs-prisma7-docker-coolify-hetzner-deployment.md`.

projects.name: OpenClaw
projects.description:
OpenClaw is a self-hosted application running on a Proxmox homelab, deployed inside a Docker container managed by Coolify on a dedicated Ubuntu VM (VM1). The setup follows a security-first posture: the VM is network-isolated using NetBird (a WireGuard-based overlay network), SSH-hardened with fail2ban and UFW, and the application is accessible only through the private NetBird network.

OpenClaw integrates with Telegram and provides optional security tooling via its ClawSec module. The repo (named `pfc` on GitHub) contains the installation guide and configuration notes for this deployment.
projects.description_short: OpenClaw is a self-hosted application running on a Proxmox homelab, deployed inside a Docker container managed by Coolify on a dedicated Ubuntu VM (VM1).
projects.hosting: Self-hosted on Proxmox homelab. VM1 at local IP 192.168.0.102 / NetBird IP 100.109.75.79. Coolify manages containers on that VM. Accessible only via NetBird private network.
projects.notes: VM1 is isolated and dedicated to OpenClaw only - do not use it for other projects (the knowledge base runs on VM2). OpenClaw docs update frequently; use Context7 to look up current OpenClaw documentation rather than relying on the CLAUDE.md content.

projects.name: Personal Knowledge Base
projects.description:
A personal semantic search and RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) system over private markdown notes. The system lets you ask natural-language questions and get answers sourced from your own documents.

The pipeline works as follows: markdown notes live on VM2 at `/home/hanna/markdown-vault/` and are edited via VS Code Remote-SSH. A Node.js indexing script uses local embeddings (`@xenova/transformers`) to chunk and embed the documents, storing them in Qdrant (a vector database deployed via Coolify). At query time, a Node.js script performs semantic search against Qdrant and sends the top chunks to the HF Inference API (Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) to generate an answer with source attribution.

A Next.js 16 web UI provides a chat interface, document management admin panel, dark mode, and markdown rendering. The UI is deployed via Coolify using a deploy key from GitHub, with nixpacks as the build system. A SQLite database (persisted via Coolify volume) tracks indexed document metadata.

This local folder (`knowledge-base-md-files/`) contains documentation and guides about the project, not the application code itself. The actual app code lives at `~/Desktop/private-knowledge-base/`.

projects.name: Private Knowledge Base
projects.description:
A personal knowledge base with semantic search and RAG over private markdown notes and documents. Three content sources feed into the system: a local `~/knowledge-base/` folder auto-synced to GitHub via `fswatch`, Google Drive folders (OAuth2, delta sync hourly / full sync every 6h), and manual drag-and-drop uploads in the admin UI.

All sources go through an ingestion pipeline that chunks content, embeds it using `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` (384-dim vectors, runs locally), and stores vectors in Qdrant. Users ask questions in a chat UI; the app retrieves relevant chunks and passes them to an LLM (Qwen 2.5 7B via HF Inference API) which streams the answer with source citations.

The web UI includes a TipTap markdown editor, a unified file sidebar showing content from all three sources (Repo / Google Drive / Uploads), and a chat interface. Deployed via Coolify on a dedicated VM (VM2) that is separate and isolated from other VMs on the home server.
projects.description_short: A personal knowledge base with semantic search and RAG over private markdown notes and documents.

The project is a pnpm monorepo with two apps: `apps/web` (Next.js frontend on Vercel) and `apps/api` (Express backend to be deployed on Coolify). Auth uses Supabase. A Vercel Cron job runs daily at 06:00 UTC to process articles via `/api/cron/process-articles`. Magic link dev login is available via `node scripts/dev-login.js` from the repo root.

projects.name: SignalStack
projects.description:
An AI-powered marketing intelligence SaaS covering SEO, AEO (Answer Engine Optimization), Google Ads monitoring, and local SEO. Built for non-technical users - natural language chat is the primary interface, not dashboards full of charts.

The two core selling points are: (1) Talk to your data - ask any marketing data a question in plain language, and (2) Your weekly action plan - cross-subsystem LangGraph agents extract top findings from each area and a consolidator synthesizes them into a ranked action plan. This "action plan" feature is the main differentiator - it replaces what an SEO agency decision-maker does.

The architecture is an npm workspaces monorepo with `apps/web` (Next.js), `apps/api` (Express on port 5000), and `packages/shared`. The Express API is a persistent server (avoids serverless timeouts for AI workloads). Auth is Supabase with JWT verified via jose + JWKS in Express middleware. Implementation plans for all 11 subsystems live in `docs/plans/`.
projects.description_short: An AI-powered marketing intelligence SaaS covering SEO, AEO (Answer Engine Optimization), Google Ads monitoring, and local SEO.

projects.name: Social Media Generator
projects.description:
A multi-agent content generator that uses LangGraph.js for agent orchestration. The system learns your writing style from previous posts and generates new content across multiple formats: blog posts, LinkedIn posts, Instagram captions, Twitter threads, and YouTube scripts.

The agent pipeline consists of specialized nodes - a topic agent, a research agent, and a writing agent - each handling a stage of content creation. Style examples stored in a library teach the system your voice. Content moves through a draft stage before being published to the library.

The app uses Supabase as the database (can run locally via `supabase start` + Docker, or against the hosted project). The LLM is Claude Sonnet via the Anthropic API (routed through `@langchain/openai` compatible interface).
